subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure of a bi-Lipschitz image of a subset of ℝⁿ (accepted theorem, reused)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, χ : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, E ⊆ ℝ^n and real numbers c₁ > 0, c₂ ≥ 0 such that c₁|a − b| ≤ |χ(a) − χ(b)| ≤ c₂|a − b| for all a, b ∈ E. Then c₁ⁿ·Lⁿ(E) ≤ Hⁿ(χ(E)) ≤ c₂ⁿ·Lⁿ(E), where Lⁿ is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^n = Euclid n and Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P (all quantities in [0, ∞]).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (χ : Euclid n → Euclid P) (E : Set (Euclid n)) (c₁ c₂ : ℝ), 0 < c₁ → 0 ≤ c₂ → (∀ a ∈ E, ∀ b ∈ E, c₁ * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖χ a - χ b‖ ∧ ‖χ a - χ b‖ ≤ c₂ * ‖a - b‖) → ENNReal.ofReal (c₁ ^ n) * volume E ≤ μHE[n] (χ '' E) ∧ μHE[n] (χ '' E) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c₂ ^ n) * volume E
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.dimred_rpd_bilipschitz_image_measure (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.regular_point_density-a1.bilipschitz_measure-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; it needs no new proof work. Role in this decomposition: the measure comparison λ(E) ≤ m_i^{-n}·Hⁿ(G_i(E)) stated in step 3 of the supplied proof (its "Optional" remark names exactly this reuse) and applied in its step 10; used by the sibling lintegral_pullback, step 0. The proof below is the one formalized there.

Notation. μH[d] is Mathlib's Hausdorff measure. By definition (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), μHE[n] = c·μH[n] on every metric space, with the same constant c := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μH[n]) ∈ [0, ∞). On ℝ^n itself, μHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. (Upper bound.) By hypothesis, χ is c₂-Lipschitz on E (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul). By the Lipschitz image inequality for Hausdorff measures (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le with d = n ≥ 0), μH[n](χ(E)) ≤ c₂ⁿ·μH[n](E). Multiplying by c gives μHE[n](χ(E)) ≤ c₂ⁿ·μHE[n](E) = c₂ⁿ·volume(E). Here c₂ⁿ = ofReal(c₂ⁿ) = (toNNReal c₂)^(n : ℝ) in [0, ∞].
2. (χ is injective on E.) If a, b ∈ E and χ(a) = χ(b), then c₁|a − b| ≤ 0. Since c₁ > 0, this forces a = b.
3. (Lower bound.) Let g := invFunOn χ E. By step 2, g(χ(a)) = a for all a ∈ E (InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn). Hence g maps χ(E) onto E (LeftInvOn.image_image). For a, b ∈ E, |g(χ(a)) − g(χ(b))| = |a − b| ≤ c₁⁻¹|χ(a) − χ(b)|, so g is c₁⁻¹-Lipschitz on χ(E). The Lipschitz image inequality gives μH[n](E) = μH[n](g(χ(E))) ≤ c₁^{−n}·μH[n](χ(E)). Multiply by c and by c₁ⁿ ∈ (0, ∞): c₁ⁿ·volume(E) = c₁ⁿ·μHE[n](E) ≤ μHE[n](χ(E)).
4. Steps 1 and 3 together are the claim.
proof_key_steps: μHE[n] = c·μH[n] with one constant c on every metric space, and μHE[n] = volume on ℝⁿ.
Upper bound: the Lipschitz image inequality for χ (constant c₂).
Lower bound: χ is injective on E, and its inverse on χ(E) is c₁⁻¹-Lipschitz; apply the Lipschitz image inequality to it.

subproblems.title: Bi-Lipschitz pieces have Borel images and pull back Hⁿ-a.e. properties (accepted theorem, reused)
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and m > 0 with m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for all a, a' ∈ B. Then F(B) is Borel. Moreover, for every predicate p on ℝ^P that holds H^n⌞F(B)-a.e. (H^n = μHE[n]), p(F(b)) holds for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B, i.e. (volume.restrict B)-a.e.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (L : NNReal) (m : ℝ), LipschitzWith L F → MeasurableSet B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, m * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F a - F a'‖) → MeasurableSet (F '' B) ∧ ∀ p : Euclid P → Prop, (∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n].restrict (F '' B)), p y) → ∀ᵐ b ∂(volume.restrict B), p (F b)
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.ptd_piece_image_measurable_ae_pullback (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.piece_tangent_density-a1.piece_pullback-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; it needs no new proof work. Role in this decomposition: the a.e. pull-back of step 3 of the supplied proof ("if a property p holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, then p(G_i(u)) holds for λ-a.e. u ∈ A_i"), together with the Borel measurability of G_i(A_i); used by the sibling piece_orientation, steps 1 and 3. The proof below is the one formalized there.

Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] on E and on ℝ^n; λ := volume on ℝ^n. On ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μHE[n] = λ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. F is injective on B. If a, a' ∈ B and F(a) = F(a'), then m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| = 0, and m > 0 gives a = a'.
2. F(B) is Borel. F is continuous (Lipschitz), ℝ^n is Polish, B is Borel and F is injective on B. So F(B) is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
3. Inverse map. Let G := Function.invFunOn F B : E → ℝ^n. For y ∈ F(B), G(y) ∈ B and F(G(y)) = y (invFunOn_pos). For y, y' ∈ F(B), m|G(y) − G(y')| ≤ |F(G(y)) − F(G(y'))| = |y − y'|. So G is m^{-1}-Lipschitz on F(B), that is, LipschitzOnWith (Real.toNNReal m^{-1}) G (F '' B). The Lipschitz image bound (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, valid between any two metric spaces with their Borel σ-algebras) gives μHE[n](G(S)) ≤ (m^{-1})^n μHE[n](S) for every S ⊆ F(B).
4. Pullback. Let p be a predicate on E with p(y) for H^n⌞F(B)-a.e. y.
- F(B) is measurable by step 2. So, by ae_restrict_iff', H^n-a.e. y satisfies y ∈ F(B) → p(y). That is, S := {y : y ∈ F(B) ∧ ¬p(y)} is H^n-null.
- Let T := {b : b ∈ B ∧ ¬p(F(b))}. If b ∈ T then y := F(b) ∈ S. Also G(y) ∈ B and F(G(y)) = F(b), so G(y) = b by step 1. Hence T ⊆ G(S).
- By step 3 and μHE[n] = λ on ℝ^n, λ(T) ≤ μHE[n](G(S)) ≤ (m^{-1})^n · 0 = 0.
- Since B is measurable, ae_restrict_iff' turns λ(T) = 0 into: p(F(b)) holds for (volume.restrict B)-a.e. b. ∎
For n = 0 every power is 1 and the argument is unchanged.
proof_key_steps: The lower bound m|a − a'| ≤ |F a − F a'| makes F injective on B.
Lusin–Souslin: F(B) is Borel.
G := invFunOn F B is m⁻¹-Lipschitz on F(B); the Lipschitz image bound gives μHE[n](G(S)) ≤ m^{-n} μHE[n](S).
The bad parameters {b ∈ B : ¬p(F b)} lie in G of the H^n-null bad image set; μHE[n] = volume on ℝ^n, and ae_restrict_iff' concludes.

subproblems.title: The carrier of a representation lies in the support up to an Hⁿ-null set (accepted theorem, reused)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (a GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) representing T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). Then H^n(M ∖ spt T) = 0, where spt T = U ∖ ⋃{W : W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, T vanishes on W} (Simon 6.2.11).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ T.support) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.support_null-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; it needs no new proof work. Role in this decomposition: the fact Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ spt X) = 0 of step 1 of the supplied proof, which the supplied proof derives from (VO) and (MR); used by the sibling support_rep, step 3. The proof below is the one formalized there.

Source: the fact "μ_T(U ∖ spt T) = 0" (Simon 6.2.11 with 6.3.1; μ_T = θH^n⌞M by 6.3.2(3)).
1. Notation. M := R.carrier ⊆ U, θ := R.mult (θ ≥ 1 on M), ξ := R.orient, μ := μHE[n].restrict M. By definition T.support = U ∖ Z with Z := T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲, where 𝒲 is the family of open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W (T ω = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W). Since M ⊆ U, M ∖ T.support = M ∩ Z.
2. Countable reduction. ℝ^P is second countable, so ⋃𝒲 = ⋃_k W_k for a countable subfamily (W_k) ⊆ 𝒲 (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable). By countable subadditivity it suffices to show H^n(M ∩ W) = 0 for one fixed W ∈ 𝒲.
3. A finite measure. C := closure W is compact and C ⊆ U, so ∫_{M ∩ C} θ dH^n < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult; since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ C) < ∞. Put ν := μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C), a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P.
4. Orientation facts. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a plane Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) spanning Q with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, s ∈ {1, −1}. At such x: (a) |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm of the continuous alternating map, since |τ_i| = 1); (b) ξ(x) ≠ 0: the n-covector β_τ(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b} (for n = 0 the constant 1) is continuous, multilinear and alternating, and β_τ(τ) = det I = 1, so ξ(x)(β_τ) = s ≠ 0.
5. Testing T. Fix an n-covector α and set f_α(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α). It is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable for μ ≥ ν) and |f_α| ≤ ‖α‖θ ν-a.e., so f_α ∈ L¹(ν). For every g ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P, ℝ) with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W, the form ω(x) := g(x)·α is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport in W. As T vanishes on W and R represents T: 0 = T ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(g(x)α) dH^n = ∫ g f_α dν (the integrand vanishes off W ⊆ C).
6. Fundamental lemma. Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero (open set W, measure ν, f_α locally integrable on W) gives: for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ θ(x)ξ(x)(α) = 0. Since θ ≥ 1 on M and ν is carried by M, ξ(x)(α) = 0 for ν-a.e. x ∈ W.
7. Conclusion. Let α_1, …, α_m be a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors on ℝ^P. Intersecting the finitely many full-measure sets of step 6, for ν-a.e. x ∈ W the linear functional ξ(x) vanishes on a basis, hence ξ(x) = 0. By step 4(b), ξ(x) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. x, hence for ν-a.e. x. Therefore ν(W) = H^n(M ∩ C ∩ W) = H^n(M ∩ W) = 0, and by step 2, H^n(M ∖ T.support) = 0.
proof_key_steps: M ∖ spt T = M ∩ zeroRegion(T), a countable union of open W ⊂⊂ U on which T vanishes.
Testing T with g·α (g ∈ C_c^∞(W), α a constant covector) gives ∫ g θ ξ(α) dH^n⌞M = 0.
The fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations gives ξ = 0 a.e. on M ∩ W, while unit orientations are nonzero; hence H^n(M ∩ W) = 0.

Source: step 1 (normalization) of the supplied proof, written for any open U (the selected theorem applies it with U := univ; the argument uses only R.carrier ⊆ U). The supplied proof derives the null-set fact Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ spt X) = 0 from (VO) and (MR). That fact is exactly the accepted sibling support_null (Submission.imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null), which is used in step 3 below. So (VO) and (MR) are not needed here; (IMC b) is the only antecedent.

Hypothesis as named in the statement: (IMC b) if U is open and E is Borel, then for every IMRep R in U there are a current A and an IMRep R' in U representing A with R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R'.mult = R.mult and R'.orient = R.orient.

Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For the current X, spt X = X.support = U ∖ X.zeroRegion by definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support), and X.zeroRegion is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion). For an IMRep R: R.action(ω) = ∫_{R.carrier} R.mult(x)·R.orient(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x).

1. (A representation.) As X is integer multiplicity, choose an IMRep R in U with R.Represents X. Write M₀ := R.carrier, θ := R.mult and ξ := R.orient.
2. (spt X is Borel.) spt X = U ∖ X.zeroRegion is the difference of two open sets (U is open by hypothesis), hence Borel.
3. (M₀ ∖ spt X is null.) By support_null (imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null with P := N, the given n and U, T := X and R; U is open and R represents X), Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ spt X) = 0.
4. (M₀ ∩ spt X equals M₀ up to a null set.) First, (M₀ ∩ spt X) ∖ M₀ = ∅. Second, M₀ ∖ (M₀ ∩ spt X) ⊆ M₀ ∖ spt X: if x ∈ M₀ and x ∉ M₀ ∩ spt X, then x ∉ spt X. By step 3 both differences are Hⁿ-null (measure_mono_null), so M₀ ∩ spt X = M₀ Hⁿ-a.e. (ae_eq_set).
5. (Restricting the representation.) Apply (IMC b) to the open set U, the IMRep R and E := spt X, which is Borel by step 2. It gives a current A and an IMRep R' in U with R'.carrier = M₀ ∩ spt X, R'.mult = θ and R'.orient = ξ. (R' represents A, but this is not needed.)
6. (R' represents X.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then R'.action(ω) = ∫_{M₀ ∩ spt X} θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ = ∫_{M₀} θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ = R.action(ω) = X(ω). The first equality uses the three identities of step 5. The second holds because set integrals over a.e.-equal sets coincide (setIntegral_congr_set with step 4); this holds for every integrand, integrable or not. The last two are the definition and R.Represents X.
7. (Carrier in the support.) R'.carrier = M₀ ∩ spt X ⊆ spt X. By steps 6 and 7, R' is the required IMRep. ∎

The basic bound (step 0 below) is the lower half of the sibling bilipschitz_measure, the accepted theorem Submission.dimred_rpd_bilipschitz_image_measure, as the supplied proof's step 3 remark anticipates.

Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P; λ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n; c := ofReal((m^n)^{-1}) ∈ [0, ∞).

0. (Basic bound.) For every E ⊆ A: λ(E) ≤ c·Hⁿ(G(E)). Indeed, let a, b ∈ E. Then m|a − b| ≤ |G(a) − G(b)| by hypothesis (E ⊆ A), and |G(a) − G(b)| = dist(G(a), G(b)) ≤ L·dist(a, b) = L|a − b| (LipschitzWith.dist_le_mul). Apply dimred_rpd_bilipschitz_image_measure with χ := G, the set E, c₁ := m > 0 and c₂ := L ≥ 0. Its first conclusion is ofReal(m^n)·λ(E) ≤ Hⁿ(G(E)). Since m^n > 0, c·ofReal(m^n) = ofReal((m^n)^{-1}·m^n) = ofReal(1) = 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). Hence λ(E) = c·(ofReal(m^n)·λ(E)) ≤ c·Hⁿ(G(E)).
1. (G is Borel.) G is Lipschitz, hence continuous, hence Borel measurable.
2. (Image measure.) Let B ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Then (G_*(λ⌞A))(B) = (λ⌞A)(G^{-1}(B)) = λ(G^{-1}(B) ∩ A) (Measure.map_apply with step 1; Measure.restrict_apply' with A Borel). The set E := G^{-1}(B) ∩ A ⊆ A satisfies G(E) ⊆ B ∩ G(A). By step 0 and monotonicity, (G_*(λ⌞A))(B) ≤ c·Hⁿ(G(E)) ≤ c·Hⁿ(B ∩ G(A)) = (c·Hⁿ⌞G(A))(B) (Measure.restrict_apply, B Borel). As this holds for every Borel B, G_*(λ⌞A) ≤ c·Hⁿ⌞G(A) as measures (Measure.le_iff).
3. (The integral bound.) Let f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] be Borel. By lintegral_map (f and G measurable), ∫_A f(G(u)) dλ(u) = ∫ f d(G_*(λ⌞A)). By step 2 and monotonicity of the integral in the measure (lintegral_mono'), this is ≤ ∫ f d(c·Hⁿ⌞G(A)). By lintegral_smul_measure, the latter equals c·∫_{G(A)} f dHⁿ. ∎

Source: step 4 (tangent planes, B2) and the measurability part of step 5 of the supplied proof, for one piece (G, A) of an arbitrary oriented Borel set M. The supplied proof applies it with M := M₀ ∩ spt X, ξ the orientation, G := G_i and A := A_i.

Hypothesis as named in the statement: (IMC a) for every P, n, every open U and all Borel M₁ ⊆ M₂ ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M₂ ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U: for Hⁿ⌞M₁-a.e. x and every subspace Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ x Q.

Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^N; λ := volume on ℝⁿ; e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a ∈ Fin n); DG(u) := fderiv ℝ G u.

1. (Pulling back a.e. statements.) By the accepted sibling ae_pullback (Submission.ptd_piece_image_measurable_ae_pullback with P := N, F := G, B := A and the given L, m): (a) G(A) is Borel; (b) every property that holds Hⁿ⌞G(A)-a.e. holds at G(u) for λ⌞A-a.e. u. Moreover, since G(A) ⊆ M, every property that holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. holds Hⁿ⌞G(A)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset).
2. (Tangent planes of the piece.) By the accepted theorem ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae (with P := N, F := G, B := A and the given L, m; its hypotheses are exactly ours), for λ⌞A-a.e. u: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (G(A)) (G(u)) (range DG(u)).
3. (Locality.) Apply (IMC a) with U := ℝ^N (open), M₁ := G(A) (Borel by 1(a)) and M₂ := M (Borel). Here G(A) ⊆ M ⊆ ℝ^N, and Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K by hypothesis. So for Hⁿ⌞G(A)-a.e. x and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (G(A)) x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. By 1(b), this holds at x = G(u) for λ⌞A-a.e. u.
4. (Orientation.) By hypothesis, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. By step 1, for λ⌞A-a.e. u there is Q_u with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (G(u)) Q_u and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(G(u))) Q_u.
5. (Identification of the plane.) Let u lie in the intersection of the three full-measure sets of steps 2, 3 and 4 (a finite intersection of λ⌞A-conull sets is conull). By step 2 and the direction ⟹ of step 3 with Q := range DG(u), M has approximate tangent space range DG(u) at G(u). By step 4, M also has approximate tangent space Q_u at G(u). Approximate tangent spaces are unique (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so Q_u = range DG(u). Further, range DG(u) = DG(u)(ℝⁿ) = DG(u)(span{e_a}) = span{DG(u)e_a : a ∈ Fin n}, because the e_a form a basis of ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose a-th vector is e_a; LinearMap.range_eq_map, Basis.span_eq, Submodule.map_span, Set.range_comp). Hence ξ(G(u)) is a unit orientation of span{DG(u)e_a : a}. This is the second conclusion.
6. (Measurability.) Since ξ is AE strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, there is a strongly measurable ξ' : ℝ^N → Λ_n(ℝ^N) with ξ = ξ' Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk and ae_eq_mk). By step 1, ξ(G(u)) = ξ'(G(u)) for λ⌞A-a.e. u. The map u ↦ ξ'(G(u)) is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.comp_measurable; G is Lipschitz, hence continuous, hence measurable). So u ↦ ξ(G(u)) is AE strongly measurable for λ⌞A, which is the first conclusion. ∎

Source: step 5 (sign, B2′) of the supplied proof, for one piece and with ζ := ξ∘G_i; the sign s_i of the supplied proof is exactly the function s constructed here.

Notation: λ := volume on ℝⁿ; e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1; DG(u) := fderiv ℝ G u (the zero map where G is not differentiable); v(u) := (DG(u)e_a)_{a ∈ Fin n} ∈ (ℝ^N)^n; J(u) := √det(⟨v_a(u), v_b(u)⟩)_{a,b}. For z ∈ (ℝ^N)^n let ev_z ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^N) = (Covector (Euclid N) n →L[ℝ] ℝ) be the evaluation functional α ↦ α(z) (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid N) ℝ z).

1. (z ↦ ev_z is continuous.) For z, z' ∈ (ℝ^N)^n and every n-covector α, |α(z) − α(z')| ≤ ‖α‖·n·max(‖z‖, ‖z'‖)^{n−1}·‖z − z'‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_image_sub_le). By the definition of the operator norm (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound), ‖ev_z − ev_{z'}‖ ≤ n·max(‖z‖, ‖z'‖)^{n−1}·‖z − z'‖. For fixed z', the right side tends to 0 as z → z'. So z ↦ ev_z is continuous.
2. (v and J are Borel.) For each a, u ↦ DG(u)e_a is Borel (measurable_fderiv_apply_const; no assumption on G is needed). Hence u ↦ v(u) ∈ (ℝ^N)^n is Borel (measurability of a map into a finite product). The map z ↦ √det(⟨z_a, z_b⟩)_{a,b} is continuous on (ℝ^N)^n (inner products, the determinant as a polynomial in the entries, the square root). So J is Borel.
3. (The comparison function.) g(u) := J(u)^{-1}·ev_{v(u)} defines a strongly measurable map ℝⁿ → Λ_n(ℝ^N). Indeed, u ↦ J(u)^{-1} is Borel and real-valued, hence strongly measurable. (ℝ^N)^n is second countable, so v is strongly measurable. Then u ↦ ev_{v(u)} is strongly measurable by step 1 (a continuous map after a strongly measurable one). Finally the scalar product of two strongly measurable maps is strongly measurable.
4. (The sign.) Let ζ' be a strongly measurable map with ζ = ζ' λ⌞A-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk, ae_eq_mk). Λ_n(ℝ^N) is a normed space, hence metrizable, so S := {u : ζ'(u) = g(u)} is Borel (StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun). Define s(u) := 1 for u ∈ S and s(u) := −1 for u ∉ S. Then s is measurable (Measurable.ite with constant branches), and s(u) ∈ {1, −1} for every u.
5. (A full-measure set.) For λ⌞A-a.e. u, the following three facts hold together: ζ(u) = ζ'(u) (step 4); ζ(u) is a unit orientation of V_u := span{v_a(u) : a} (hypothesis); and u ∈ A (ae_restrict_mem, A Borel). Fix such u and an n-covector α.
